## archive then remove idle unmerged lanes

ID: `lane-sweep/archive-then-remove-idle-unmerged-lanes`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/lane_sweep.py` SHALL remove the worktree of a lane whose content is not on the remote default branch when it passes every other check of "Remove finished lanes and report the rest" (clean, ignored non-cache files under 1 MiB, not in use by a process or a systemd user unit, not locked, not passed as `--keep-lane`, no submodules) and has been idle for at least the archive limit: 72 hours, or the number of hours in `lane_sweep_archive_after_hours:` in `graph-config.yaml` (`$LANE_SWEEP_ARCHIVE_AFTER_HOURS`, `--archive-after-hours`); 0 or less SHALL turn this off. `--merged-lane` SHALL NOT shorten this wait. Before any move it SHALL preserve the tip: when no remote-tracking branch holds the tip, it SHALL create the local ref `refs/archive/<YYYYMMDD>/<lane folder name>` at the tip with `git update-ref` refusing to overwrite (a name already taken by another commit gets `-<tip>` appended), write a `git bundle` of that ref and the lane's branch holding only the commits not on the remote default branch into the log folder, and run `git bundle verify` on it. A detached lane SHALL get the local ref even when a remote-tracking branch holds its tip. When creating the ref, the bundle or its verification fails, the lane SHALL be kept whole and the sweep SHALL exit 1. The ref SHALL be pushed to origin only when origin's GitHub owner is the `owner:` setting and GitHub, asked through that owner's gh wrapper, reports the repository private; a failed push SHALL be logged and SHALL NOT stop the removal. The removal SHALL then run as in "Remove finished lanes and report the rest", except that the local branch SHALL be kept. The day's log SHALL name the branch, the tip, the bundle and the command `git -C <repo> worktree add <path> <branch, or the archive ref when detached>` that restores the lane, and SHALL list the ignored files the removal deletes, other than rebuildable caches such as `.venv`. Without `--apply` the lane SHALL only be listed as archivable, with no ref and no bundle written.

## fast forward primary checkouts that are clean and idle

ID: `lane-sweep/fast-forward-primary-checkouts-that-are-clean-and-idle`

Status: **implemented and tested**

After judging a repository's lanes, `scripts/lane_sweep.py` SHALL fast-forward the repository's primary checkout (the main worktree, the parent of `--git-common-dir`) to the remote default branch with `git merge --ff-only`, and only when all hold: the checkout is on the branch that the remote default branch tracks; `git status --porcelain` is empty (ignored files do not count); the local branch is a strict ancestor of the remote default branch after the sweep's fetch; no git command holds the checkout's `index.lock`; and no running process outside the sweep's own ancestors and session has its working directory inside the checkout, not counting processes inside a linked worktree nested in it. It SHALL never reset or rebase the checkout. Each fast-forward SHALL append the checkout, branch, old commit and new commit to the day's log. A checkout that is behind but not moved SHALL be listed with the reason. Without `--apply` it SHALL only list the checkout as fast-forwardable. Repositories with no lanes SHALL be fetched and judged too. A checkout whose root folder is read-only (`canonical_lock.py` locked it while a lane claim is live) SHALL be moved with `canonical_lock.py --sync` (unlock, `git pull --ff-only`, re-lock) instead of `git merge`.

## keep lanes that a systemd user unit runs from

ID: `lane-sweep/keep-lanes-that-a-systemd-user-unit-runs-from`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/lane_sweep.py` SHALL keep a lane, and report it with the unit's name, when any systemd user unit names a path inside it in a unit file or a drop-in (`<unit>.service.d/*.conf`), on any line (for example `WorkingDirectory`, `ExecStart` or `Environment`), whether or not a process is running from it. It SHALL read every folder systemd loads user units from: `~/.config/systemd/user`, the transient folder `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/transient` (`/run/user/<uid>` when the variable is unset), the runtime `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/user`, `~/.local/share/systemd/user` and `/etc/systemd/user`. A timer's job is no process until the timer fires, and `systemd-run --user --on-calendar` writes its unit only to the transient folder, so reading `~/.config/systemd/user` alone lets the sweep remove a lane that a scheduled run will start from.

## keep locked worktrees

ID: `lane-sweep/keep-locked-worktrees`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/lane_sweep.py` SHALL keep a worktree that git reports as locked (`git worktree lock`), whatever else is true of it, and SHALL report it as locked, with the lock's reason when one was given. A lock is how a tool marks a worktree that is not a lane, such as a pinned checkout another project's Python environment imports from: with no process running, such a worktree passes every other check and looks like a finished lane.

## remove finished lanes and report the rest

ID: `lane-sweep/remove-finished-lanes-and-report-the-rest`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/lane_sweep.py` SHALL, for every linked worktree of each repository it is given (default: every repository under `~/code2`), remove the worktree and delete its local branch only when all hold: the tree has no uncommitted changes (ignored files do not count); its content is on the remote default branch, meaning the branch tip is an ancestor of it, or every file the branch changed has the same content there, or a merged pull request's head on GitHub is exactly the branch tip; no running process outside the sweep's own ancestors and session (the command that launched it) uses the worktree, meaning its working directory, a command-line argument, an open or mapped file, a code search path in its environment (`PYTHONPATH`, `VIRTUAL_ENV` and similar) or an absolute path in a `.pth` file of the Python environment it runs from is inside the worktree; and the worktree has been idle for at least 30 minutes, or 24 hours when the branch has no commits of its own; and its ignored files that are not regenerable caches total under 1 MiB (1048576 bytes), where a cache is anything under a folder named `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.tox`, `dist`, `build`, `.cache`, `.next`, `target`, `.lockstep`, `.code2check` or `.work`, or an `.egg-info` folder, at any depth; a size that cannot be read SHALL count as reaching the limit. A lane failing only this check SHALL be kept with the reason `holds ignored non-cache files: <up to 5 paths>`, because `git worktree remove` deletes ignored files even without `--force`; a removed lane's smaller ignored non-cache files SHALL be listed in the day's log. Every other lane SHALL be kept and listed with the reason, except an idle lane whose content is not on the remote default branch, which the requirement "Archive then remove idle unmerged lanes" governs. Each removal SHALL append the branch name, its tip and the command that restores the branch to one log file per day. Removal SHALL first move the worktree aside with `git worktree move` to the hidden sibling `.<name>.lane-sweep-removing`, so the lane's own path disappears in one step, and SHALL then run `git worktree remove` without `--force`. When the move fails nothing is changed. When a process uses the moved tree, a folder in it cannot be written, or the removal fails while the moved tree's tracked files are intact, it SHALL be moved back. When the removal fails after deleting files, the remains SHALL stay at the hidden path, the branch SHALL be kept, and the log SHALL name the command that recreates the lane; a later sweep SHALL keep and list such a hidden path. A git command that times out SHALL count as a failed step and SHALL NOT stop the sweep. Without `--apply` it SHALL only report. Worktree records whose folder is gone SHALL be pruned. `scripts/ship.py` SHALL run the sweep for its repository right after the pull request reads back MERGED, passing its own lane as `--merged-lane` so that lane skips only the idle wait; a failed sweep SHALL NOT fail the ship.

## settings come from config

ID: `lane-sweep/settings-come-from-config`

Status: **implemented and tested**

The gh command that asks GitHub for a merged pull request SHALL be `$LANE_SWEEP_GH` when set, else the wrapper `github_accounts:` in `graph-config.yaml` (beside `$PROJECT_GRAPH`, default `~/code2/aes-config/PROJECT_GRAPH.json`) names for the repository's owner, else the one it names for the top-level `owner:`, else `gh`. The canonical-lock tool SHALL be `$LANE_SWEEP_CANONICAL_LOCK`, else the `canonical_lock:` key; when neither names one, a primary checkout moves with `git merge --ff-only`. Settings SHALL be read when needed, never at import, so a machine without the file still sweeps.
